title: Checkpoint
description: Past-paper data processing checkpoints using extracted question prompts and marking points.

questions.title: Checkpoint 1 - Largest and Average Excluding Largest
questions.question: Q2(c)
questions.context:
A program will:
- input 50 unique integer values
- output the largest value
- output the average of the values excluding the largest value.
questions.task:
Draw a program flowchart to represent the algorithm.
Variable declarations are not required.
It is not necessary to check that each input value is unique.
expectedThinking: Initialise MAX to the first value input
Set Total to zero before accumulation
Update MAX when a larger value is found
Calculate average excluding MAX and output results

markScheme.criterion: Initialise MAX from an input value
Update MAX when input > MAX in loop
Exclude largest from average and output

assessment.expectedAnswer:
DECLARE Value, MAX, Total : INTEGER
DECLARE Average : REAL
DECLARE Index : INTEGER

Total <- 0
INPUT Value
MAX <- Value
Total <- Total + Value

FOR Index <- 2 TO 50
    INPUT Value
    Total <- Total + Value
    IF Value > MAX THEN
        MAX <- Value
    ENDIF
NEXT Index

Average <- (Total - MAX) / 49
OUTPUT MAX
OUTPUT Average

questions.title: Checkpoint 2 - Odd/Even Indexed Totals in Array
questions.question: Q4
questions.context:
A global 1D array Data contains 100 elements of type integer.
A function Check() will:
- total the element values in odd index locations (1, 3, 5 ... 97, 99)
- total the element values in even index locations (2, 4, 6 ... 98, 100)
- return one of three strings "Odd", "Even" or "Same" to indicate which total is greater, or whether the totals are the same.
questions.task: Write pseudocode for the function Check().
expectedThinking: Declare integer totals for odd and even index groups
Use MOD 2 to identify odd or even index
Accumulate into the correct running total
Compare totals and return the correct string

markScheme.criterion: Declare local variables Odd, Even, Index

assessment.expectedAnswer:
FUNCTION Check() RETURNS STRING
DECLARE Odd, Even, Index : INTEGER
Odd <- 0
Even <- 0

FOR Index <- 1 TO 100
    IF Index MOD 2 = 0 THEN
        Even <- Even + Data[Index]
    ELSE
        Odd <- Odd + Data[Index]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index

IF Odd > Even THEN
    RETURN "Odd"
ELSE
    IF Even > Odd THEN
        RETURN "Even"
    ELSE
        RETURN "Same"
    ENDIF
ENDIF
ENDFUNCTION

questions.title: Checkpoint 3 - Loyalty Points Reporting
questions.question: Q7(b)
questions.pattern: 2D array scan with condition and aggregate
questions.context:
A program is being developed to implement a customer loyalty scheme for a coffee shop.

Each customer has a unique customer ID starting at 10001, increasing by one each time a new customer joins the loyalty scheme.

The loyalty scheme is limited to 1000 customers.

A customer is awarded a loyalty point every time they buy a coffee.

A global 2D array Loyalty of type INTEGER is used.
Loyalty has 1000 rows and 2 columns.
Each row relates to one customer:
- column 1 stores the unique customer ID
- column 2 stores the number of customer loyalty points

Rows in the Loyalty array that are not currently being used have column 1 set to 99999.

The array is sorted in ascending order by customer ID.

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| FindCustomer() | - called with an INTEGER parameter representing a customer ID\n- searches the Loyalty array for this customer ID\n- the search stops as soon as the customer ID is found\n- efficiently handles when the customer ID is not stored\n- returns loyalty points if found, otherwise returns -1 |
questions.task:
A customer can claim a free coffee for every 11 loyalty points.

| Module | Description |
| --- | --- |
| PointsReport() | - output the customer ID for each customer who has 11 or more loyalty points\n- output the average loyalty points for all customers in the Loyalty array with an appropriate message |

Write efficient pseudocode for module PointsReport().
Assume the array contains the data for at least one customer.
expectedThinking: Iterate through valid rows in Loyalty
Stop at sentinel value 99999 in column 1 (or row limit)
Accumulate total points and customer count
Calculate and output average with a message

markScheme.criterion: Declare and initialise Index, Sum, Count
Terminate loop at 99999 (or equivalent bound-safe stop)
Check points >= 11 and output customer ID
Calculate and output average with message

assessment.expectedAnswer:
PROCEDURE PointsReport()
DECLARE Count : INTEGER
DECLARE Index : INTEGER
DECLARE Sum : INTEGER
DECLARE Average : REAL

Index <- 1
Count <- 0
Sum <- 0

WHILE Loyalty[Index, 1] <> 99999 AND Index <= 1000
    IF Loyalty[Index, 2] >= 11 THEN
        OUTPUT Loyalty[Index, 1]
    ENDIF

    Count <- Count + 1
    Sum <- Sum + Loyalty[Index, 2]
    Index <- Index + 1
ENDWHILE

Average <- Sum / Count
OUTPUT "The average points of all the customers is ", Average
ENDPROCEDURE
